soldier: Body rather large. Head reddish brown, the antennae and pronotum reddish yellow, the mandibles dark brown with reddish brown bases. Long bristles scattered over the head; the periphery and the posterior half of the pronotum bear numerous erect, stout, long bristles; about ten stout long setae around the margin of the labrum; the anterior half of the postmentum with several setae of unequal length. The head is slightly rectangular-trapezoidal, narrower anteriorly, widest at about the posterior third, the posterior margin slightly arcuate. Mandibles very robust, the apices slightly incurved; the tooth of the left mandible rather large, at about one-third from the anterior end; the tooth of the right mandible very small, merely a point, situated slightly below the left marginal tooth, with another small tooth near the base. Labrum lingulate, reaching the middle of the mandibles. Antennae with 16–17 segments, mostly 17, segment 3 the shortest in most individuals. The anterior margin of the pronotum has a rather broad notch, and the middle of the posterior margin is distinctly concave.
taxonomy_note: The original work records this as Odontotermes shanglinensis; it is now merged, as a synonym, into O. longzhouensis.
worker: The worker has a large and a small form. In the large worker the bristles of the head are longer and more numerous, head width 1.63–1.67 mm, pronotal width 0.92–0.96 mm, antennae with 18 segments, segment 4 short and small. In the small worker the bristles of the head are fewer, head width 1.08–1.13 mm, pronotal width 0.71–0.75 mm, antennae with 17 segments, segments 3, 4 and 5 short and small and approximately equal to one another.
